stem: A term newborn becomes pink and starts breathing well after delivery. Which haemodynamic change is expected as part of normal postnatal transition?

options.text: Pulmonary vascular resistance falls and systemic vascular resistance rises
Pulmonary vascular resistance rises and systemic vascular resistance falls
Right atrial pressure rises above left atrial pressure, keeping the foramen ovale open
The ductus venosus remains the main pathway for umbilical venous return for 2 to 3 weeks
Left ventricular dominance is expected in the neonatal period

explanation: Pulmonary vascular resistance falls and systemic vascular resistance rises. This is the expected haemodynamic change after birth when the lungs expand and placental circulation is removed, supporting normal postnatal transition.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because lung expansion lowers pulmonary vascular resistance and removal of the placenta increases systemic vascular resistance after birth.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the normal postnatal transition is the opposite: pulmonary vascular resistance falls and systemic vascular resistance rises.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the foramen ovale closes when left atrial pressure exceeds right atrial pressure after birth.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the ductus venosus closes shortly after birth when umbilical venous flow stops.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the neonatal circulation is characterised by right ventricular dominance, not left ventricular dominance.
